sections.title: Social Impact Lab - TRAVEL COURSE
sections.description: NPLD 5850 is a 5-day, off-site, intensive residential course in social innovation. This course will explore the intersections of passion, purpose, and social impact. Students will learn how social innovators co-develop new ideas with key stakeholders, articulate problems and solutions, define intended impact, and collaborate with other actors -- while also examining the values, skills, and interests that set the foundation for their own careers. This course thus involves both self-exploration, the study of the many pathways to social impact, and reflections on the intersection of the two. At the end of the course, students will have learned a set of conceptual tools and strategies that will allow them to be effective problem solvers in diverse settings and answered a set of purpose-driven questions to articulate a plan for future personal and professional growth in the social impact sector.

sections.title: Social Impact Lab - TRAVEL COURSE
sections.description: NPLD 5850 is a 5-day, off-site, intensive service-learning course in social innovation. Students will learn how innovation and entrepreneurship play a central role in public problem solving. The course will explore how social entrepreneurs co-develop new ideas with key stakeholders, articulate problems and solutions, define intended impact, understand competition, and collaborate with other actors. At the end of the course, students will have mastered a set of conceptual tools and strategies that will allow them to be effective problem solvers in diverse settings throughout their careers. The course has five core objectives: 1) To introduce students to the concepts and practices of social entrepreneurship; 2) To introduce students to the components of a successful social enterprise; 3) To train students to view the world from a perspective of social innovation; 4) To encourage and empower students to develop their own innovative solutions to different social problems around the world. 5) To introduce students to real social issues and social innovations in a real-world setting.
